routes.title: Model routes
routes.lede: Every login and API key that serves each model, in priority order, with the cooldowns Provimux recorded on them.
routes.load_failed: Could not load the model routes
routes.note: Among the routes that can serve a new request, a higher priority is tried first, and routes that share a priority are chosen between by the routing strategy; a session already on a route may stay there. A recorded cooldown is the timer Provimux wrote after a refused request, with its reason. It is not an availability verdict: a route without one can still fail (an expired login, for one), and Auth Files shows each login's state.
routes.empty_text: Sign a login in on OAuth Login, or add an API key on AI Providers; its models appear here.
routes.tier_shared: Priority {{priority}}: {{count}} routes share it; the routing strategy chooses between them
routes.tier_unknown: Priority not reported by the server

devin.title: Devin: quota pause per model
devin.eyebrow: When a Devin login runs out of its daily or weekly quota
devin.on_text: On: only the model Devin refused is paused until the quota resets; Devin keeps serving the models it does not meter (swe-2, swe-2-flash).
devin.off_text: Off: the whole login pauses until the quota resets, including the models Devin keeps serving without a quota (swe-2, swe-2-flash). Turn it on to pause only the refused model.
devin.limit_note: Known limit: Provimux may not learn the quota's reset time, so a paused model retries with a growing backoff (1 second up to 30 minutes, one quick refused request each time).
devin.saved_on: Devin pauses only the refused model now
devin.saved_off: Devin pauses the whole login again
devin.none_cooling: No cooldown recorded on the Devin login ({{count}} models).
devin.absent_no_login: No Devin login. The switch applies when you add one.
devin.absent_enabled_no_routes: No registered Devin routes: the Devin login is enabled but serves no model (are its models excluded?).
devin.absent_disabled: No registered Devin routes: the Devin login is disabled.

openrouter.title: OpenRouter, built in
openrouter.eyebrow: OpenAI Compatible entries whose base URL is on openrouter.ai
openrouter.text: Provimux adds prompt-cache markers to requests that have none, keeps one conversation on one upstream with an X-Session-Id header, and gives each model its own context, output limit and reasoning levels from OpenRouter's model list. Nothing to configure.
openrouter.empty: No OpenRouter entry yet. On AI Providers, add an OpenAI Compatible provider with this base URL and your OpenRouter key:
openrouter.limits_line: Show the {{count}} OpenRouter routes and their limits ({{sample}})
openrouter.limits_line_one: Show the OpenRouter route and its limits ({{sample}})
openrouter.limits_line_other: Show the {{count}} OpenRouter routes and their limits ({{sample}})
openrouter.tag_title: Provimux's OpenRouter support: cache markers, a session header, OpenRouter's own limits. Open its models on Model routes.

live.title: Live model lists
live.lede: Each Claude, Codex and Meta login can register the models its own account lists, not only the shared catalog: retired models disappear and new ones appear the day the provider lists them.
live.load_failed: Could not load the live lists
live.on_text: On: each login asks its provider for its model list at startup, every 3 hours and when you refresh. Until a list arrives, or while fetches fail, the catalog or the last good list is used, so an outage never empties a login. A login file replaced by another account never keeps the old list.
live.off_text: Off: every login uses the built-in catalog. Turn it on to have each Claude, Codex and Meta login register what its own account lists. It applies at once.
live.refresh_hint: Asks the server to refresh the model catalogs and each login's list in the background. Each row below shows its login's state as of the latest status read.
live.refresh_off_hint: Turn live lists on to refresh them.
live.refresh_requested: Refresh requested at {{time}}. Each row below shows its login's state as of the latest status read; Reload reads it again.
live.refresh_catalog_failed: The server could not refresh the model catalog ({{message}}). Each row below shows its login's state as of the latest status read; Reload reads it again.
live.refresh_unconfirmed: Could not confirm the refresh request — the server may still be refreshing; the rows below update on the next status read.
live.saved_off: Live lists are off; every login uses the catalog
live.empty_title: No login with a live list
live.empty_text: Live lists cover logins of {{providers}}. Sign one in on OAuth Login.
live.state_live: The provider's list for this account filters its models.
live.state_live_failing: The newest fetch failed; the previous list is kept and is getting old.
live.state_disabled: The login is disabled; it is never fetched.
live.state_failed: No list yet: the latest fetch failed, so the catalog is used.
live.state_waiting: No list yet: the first fetch has not finished.
live.state_unknown: A model source this console does not know.

hint.provider_error: The provider answered with an error.
hint.http_other: The provider answered with an error status.
hint.credentials: Provimux could not prepare the login's credentials.
hint.network: The provider could not be reached.
hint.invalid_response: The provider's answer was not a usable model list.
hint.other: The fetch failed for another reason.

live.note: Live lists cover logins of {{providers}}; other providers and every API key keep the catalog. A failed fetch is retried; its reason in words is in the server's log. Fetch times are the server's.

savings.title: Savings
savings.lede: What prompt caching was worth at API list prices, how many requests subscriptions and API keys served, and what the API keys really cost. Every amount marked estimate is at list prices.

basis.label: What these numbers cover
basis.rates_base: at base rates (long-context tiers not applied)

headline.title: Worth of prompt caching
headline.text: Valued at API list prices, net of what writing the cache cost: every input token at the input price, minus what the cached mix cost. Only the part on API keys is money saved.
headline.apikey_text: money that would have been paid
headline.oauth_text: saves quota, not dollars; value at list price
headline.negative: Caching cost more than it was worth in this period: the cache was written and not read enough to pay for the writes.
headline.unvalued: No amount: nothing in this period has a price, so nothing can be valued.
headline.partial: Only the {{priced}} of {{requests}} requests with a price are in this amount. It is not a lower bound: a request without a price can be worth less than nothing, because writing the cache costs more than plain input.
headline.text_base: Valued at base API list prices, net of what writing the cache cost: every input token at the input price, minus what the cached mix cost. Only the part on API keys is money saved.

unpriced.title: Not in the amounts

state.nothing_recorded: Provimux records from the moment this version started. Totals appear with the first request; nothing from before can be shown.
state.nothing_in_period: No requests in this period. Data exists since {{day}}.
state.floating: {{count}} requests are valued with today's list: their day has no recorded price yet (recorded without one, or not saved yet), so their amounts can still move.
state.floating_one: {{count}} request is valued with today's list: its day has no recorded price yet (recorded without one, or not saved yet), so its amounts can still move.
state.floating_other: {{count}} requests are valued with today's list: their day has no recorded price yet (recorded without one, or not saved yet), so their amounts can still move.
state.no_price_list: No price list yet, so nothing can be valued: Provimux downloads OpenRouter's public list when it records requests. Requests, tokens and the hit rate are shown as usual.
state.no_price_list_local: No price list: this Provimux runs with --local-model and does not download OpenRouter's list, so nothing can be valued. Requests, tokens and the hit rate are shown as usual.
state.not_persistent: Not being saved: these totals are in memory only and end with the next restart. The local store is off (server.kv-store.disabled), or a write to it failed.
state.folded_days: On {{count}} days the row limit was reached: some models and keys of those days are summed under "other".
state.folded_days_one: On {{count}} day the row limit was reached: some models and keys of that day are summed under "other".
state.folded_days_other: On {{count}} days the row limit was reached: some models and keys of those days are summed under "other".

savings.attempts: A request is one attempt at one upstream: a request retried on another account counts twice.
savings.note: Estimates are at list prices of the day each request was recorded: OpenRouter's public list, and Provimux's own table for models it lacks. A reported cost is what the provider said it charged. Days are the server's.
savings.note_base: Estimates are at base list prices of the day each request was recorded (long-context tiers not applied): OpenRouter's public list, and Provimux's own table for models it lacks. A reported cost is what the provider said it charged. Days are the server's.
